text: Van der Poel seized the finale with a brilliant attack over Montmartre, holding off a furious late charge from the sprinters all the way to the Champs-Élysées to claim the stage—a statement of intent that underscored his dominance through the Tour's closing kilometers. Pogačar's stranglehold on yellow remained unchallenged, but Evenepoel's late aggression on the climb proved enough to confirm second overall, a result he clearly felt vindicated a season of doubt. The stage's revised route, shortened due to wildfires southwest of Paris, only compressed the drama: one final climb, one final chance, and Van der Poel took it.
